# Style onto a set of cards, structure held

**Workflow:** [`tarot/tarot-style-transfer.json`](../tarot/tarot-style-transfer.json)

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Family | `tarot` |
| Nodes | 8 |
| Links | 8 |
| Paid API calls per run | **2 per input** |
| Reads | `tarot/base` |
| Writes | `tarot/styled` |

---

Each card keeps its own composition; one reference image lends the look to all of them.

**Top lane — FLUX.2 [pro].** *Load Images From Directory* emits a **list**, so the [pro] node fires once per card. The card goes into `input_image` (the thing being redrawn) and the style reference into `input_image_2`. Slot order is the whole instruction here: the prompt names which is which, so say it explicitly and keep it consistent.

`disable_pup` is **on**. Prompt upsampling rewrites your wording, and a style prompt you have tuned over several runs is exactly the thing you do not want rewritten.

The `filenames` output is wired to the save node's `label`, so `the-tower.png` comes back as `styled_the-tower.png` rather than `styled_0007.png`. That is what makes a run reversible — you can always tell which card a result came from.

**Bottom lane — Stability Style Transfer.** The same two images with explicit dials instead of a prompt:

- `style_strength` — how much of the reference's look lands.
- `composition_fidelity` — how hard the original composition is held. This is the one to raise when a card's structure starts drifting.
- `change_strength` — how far from the init image it may travel at all.

Run both on one card first and compare. They fail differently: FLUX.2 tends to reinterpret, Stability tends to recolour.

### Cost
One API call per card, per lane. Point `directory` at three cards before pointing it at seventy-eight.
